questions.heading: A Row Binds When the Plan Leaves It No Slack
questions.stem: A utility's selection MILP has a row once_R7: the start variables of project R7 sum to at most 1. The report of the optimal plan lists once_R7 among the rows with zero slack. What does that tell a planner about R7?

options.text: R7 is in the plan; the row records that choice and need not be holding anything back
options.says: Right: an at-most-once row has zero slack exactly when its project is funded. Binding here means chosen, not limiting.

options.text: R7 is out of the plan; the row has no slack because none of its start variables is used
options.says: With every start variable at 0 the row's activity is 0 and its slack is 1, so it would not be listed.

options.text: R7 is in the plan; the row is costing value at the margin and is worth relaxing first
options.says: Zero slack alone says nothing about cost at the margin; on GridCap 23 such rows bind just because their projects were chosen.

options.text: R7 is out of the plan; the row is what stopped the solver from choosing it in any year
options.says: A funded project is what makes this row tight; an unfunded one leaves it with slack 1.

questions.heading: A MILP Has No Prices, and Binding Means Zero Slack Even When the Price Is Zero
questions.stem: In the LP relaxation of a planning model, the row cap_2029 has slack 0 and shadow price 0 at the optimum. A colleague's report leaves it off the binding list. Who is right, and why?

options.text: The colleague, since a binding row must also carry a nonzero price
options.says: Binding asks only for zero slack: must_P003 binds in the LP relaxation with a price of 0.

options.text: The report, since zero slack is all it takes; the price shows degeneracy
options.says: Right: binding means zero slack. A binding row priced at zero is the mark of degeneracy, as must_P003 showed.

options.text: The colleague, since a zero price means the row still has room left
options.says: Complementary slackness runs the other way: room left forces a zero price, but a zero price does not force room.

options.text: The report, since every row at an LP optimum has zero slack and price
options.says: GridCap's LP relaxation had 16 rows with slack and many binding rows with nonzero prices.

questions.heading: On a MILP, a Row With Slack Can Still Be the Row That Blocks
questions.stem: A MILP's best plan leaves $40k unspent in 2028. Every unfunded project needs at least $90k in 2028 in every start year open to it. How should the binding report describe budget_2028?

options.text: Neither binding nor blocking, since $40k of slack is room to spare
options.says: Whole projects cannot use the last $40k; the row refuses every addition that needs money in 2028.

options.text: Binding, since a slack of $40k is within the solver's tolerance of zero
options.says: Tolerances are around 1e-6 of a unit, not $40k; the row has slack and so does not bind.

options.text: Not binding, yet it refuses every addition that needs 2028 money
options.says: Right: slack is positive, so the row does not bind, yet no remaining project fits in it.

options.text: Binding, since every budget row of a MILP's optimal plan has zero slack
options.says: GridCap small's best plan has slack in all five budget rows, $50k to $150k.
